title: From a canvas to a ninety-second pitch

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Here's a challenge: explain your startup idea in ninety seconds, out loud, with no slides. That was one of the exercises in QcES, an entrepreneurship program Antoine joined in spring 2024.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No slides at all? That sounds scary.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's meant to force clarity early. The program covered a whole toolkit, and his post is a personal recap of it. It starts with the Business Model Canvas, a one-page map with nine blocks: who you serve, what you promise, channels, revenue, and so on.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So you fill it in once and you're done?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, and that's the point. You state a hypothesis, talk to people, adjust your customer segments and value proposition, then decide what goes on a roadmap. The canvas moves when the market moves.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why talk to people so much?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Interviews were the heart of the cohort for Antoine. They fill the gaps a first canvas always has. You don't pitch your fix on the call. You learn how the other person lives the problem. The line he still repeats is: fall in love with the problem, not the solution.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Beyond the ideal customer too: users of substitutes, experts, suppliers, communities. Segmentation helps. Splitting business customers from consumers turns a vague label like doctors or parents into a group you can actually find and email.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What about proof of concept, prototype, MVP? They always get mixed up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three different beats. A proof of concept asks whether the approach can work. A prototype explores how people interact with it. An MVP is the smallest version you put in front of real users, to learn fast.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hook, Believe, Join. Hook with the problem and why it matters. Believe with your solution, what makes it different, and evidence like traction or team. Join with a specific ask: money, expertise, an introduction.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Any advice he'd give a founder friend?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Run five interviews with the same script, update the canvas once with real evidence, and practice the ninety-second pitch aloud. Consistency beats polish. The full write-up has the canvas flow and a week-by-week table.
